description: The reference-point method returns Pareto-optimal paths one at a time, the closest to a target first. The user gives an *aspiration point* `r` (the costs they hope for) and positive weights `w`. Closeness is the *achievement* `max_i w_i · (c_i − r_i)`, a weighted Chebyshev distance. The search is best-first on the achievement of `f = g + h`, a lower bound because the achievement is monotone. Each call of `next` continues the same search, and `aim` moves the point or the weights without lost work, so a person can steer the search interactively.

papers.title: The Use of Reference Objectives in Multiobjective Optimization
